page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m4.xlarge is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.e server family. It is configured with 4 vCPUs allocated on a shared basis, utilizing 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 4.0 GB memory-per-core ratio, and does not feature any local storage or GPU hardware. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but weak multi-core scaling, likely due to the shared CPU allocation model. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores fall into the average tier, while multi-core metrics from stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark are classified as weak. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for uncached large-block reads and writes, but weak performance for cached small-block reads.

Given the shared CPU architecture and lack of dedicated local storage, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads with low resource density or intermittent CPU demands. It is best suited for general-purpose tasks, light text processing, basic development environments, and low-traffic web serving where sustained multi-core performance is not a critical requirement.
